sentiment.rationale: Forward guidance was raised materially: Q3 revenue guided to $54B ±2%, above the $53.1B consensus and the company's own prior trajectory, while assuming zero H20 China revenue (making the raise organic). Management expressed high confidence ('demand is extraordinary,' 'record quarter,' 'industrial revolution'), and the $3–4 trillion decade-long AI infrastructure outlook extends the runway narrative. Deductions for a second consecutive slight Data Center miss ($41.1B vs $41.34B street) and growth deceleration to +56% YoY, but the net forward signal is strongly positive.

summary.eps: Non-GAAP EPS $1.05 vs $1.01 consensus; GAAP EPS $1.08 (includes ~$2.2B non-operating equity gains).
summary.guidance: Q3 revenue guided to $54.0B ±2%, above $53.1B consensus, assuming zero H20 China shipments. Longer-term: '$3 to $4 trillion in AI infrastructure spend by the end of the decade.'
summary.margin: Non-GAAP gross margin 72.7% (72.3% ex-H20 reserve release), above outlook. Q3 guided to 73.5% ±50bps, with expectation to 'exit the year with non-GAAP gross margins in the mid-70% range.'
key_risks: Data Center revenue $41.1B slightly below $41.34B StreetAccount consensus, the second consecutive optical miss.
Compute revenue declined 1% QoQ due to $4B H20 hole.
Growth deceleration to +56% YoY, the slowest in the nine-quarter >50% streak.
China H20 revenue fully de-risked in guide; $2–5B contingent upside depends on unresolved geopolitical issues and uncodified 15% USG revenue share.
Inventory +33% QoQ to $15.0B; purchase commitments $45.8B; DSO up 46→54 days.
ASIC competition and power constraints raised in Q&A.
key_opportunities: Blackwell Ultra (GB300) production ramping at full speed; demand described as 'extraordinary.'
Networking record $7.3B, +98% YoY; Spectrum-X Ethernet annualized >$10B.
Sovereign AI revenue on track to exceed $20B this year, more than double last year.
China market estimated at 'above $50 billion of opportunity for us this year' if addressable, growing ~50%/year.
Reasoning/agentic AI driving orders-of-magnitude compute demand; enterprise AI adoption opening.
Physical AI and robotics as new long-term demand driver.
$60B share repurchase authorization added; $10B returned in Q2.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Jensen Huang stated 'Blackwell is the AI platform the world has been waiting for... demand is extraordinary,' and Colette Kress described 'the beginning of an industrial revolution,' reflecting strong conviction in the growth trajectory.

evidence.claim: Revenue was a record $46.74B, +56% YoY, beating consensus.
evidence.quote: Total revenue was $46.7 billion, exceeded our outlook as we grew sequentially across all market platforms. Data center revenue grew 56% year-over-year.
Non-GAAP EPS $1.05 vs $1.01 LSEG — beat ($1.04 excluding a $180M H20 reserve release).

evidence.claim: Q3 revenue guidance raised to $54B ±2%, above consensus, assuming zero H20 China.
evidence.quote: Total revenue is expected to be $54 billion plus or minus 2%. This represents over $7 billion in sequential growth. Again, we do not assume any H20 shipments to China customers in our outlook.

evidence.claim: Non-GAAP gross margin 72.7%, above outlook; Q3 guided to 73.5% with mid-70s exit expected.
evidence.quote: GAAP gross margin was 72.4% and non-GAAP gross margin was 72.7%. These figures include a $180 million, or 40 basis point benefit from releasing previously reserved H20 inventory. Excluding this benefit, non-GAAP gross margins would have been 72.3%, still exceeding our outlook. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 73.3%, 73.5%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. We continue to expect to exit the year with non-GAAP gross margins in the mid-70s.

evidence.claim: Data Center revenue $41.1B slightly below $41.34B consensus, second consecutive optical miss.
evidence.quote: Data Center $41.1B vs $41.34B StreetAccount consensus — a slight optical miss, the second straight; compute declined 1% QoQ on the $4.0B H20 hole.

evidence.claim: Growth deceleration to +56% YoY, slowest in nine-quarter streak.
evidence.quote: Growth overall decelerating — +56% YoY is the slowest in the nine-quarter >50% streak.

evidence.claim: China H20 revenue fully de-risked in guide; $2–5B contingent upside depends on geopolitics.
evidence.quote: We have not included H20 in our Q3 outlook as we continue to work through geopolitical issues. If geopolitical issues reside, we should ship $2 billion to $5 billion in H20 revenue in Q3, and if we add more orders, we can bill more.
To support the ramp of Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra, inventory increased sequentially from $11 billion to $15 billion in Q2.

Networking delivered record revenue of $7.3 billion... This represents a 46% sequential and 98% year-on-year increase... Spectrum-X Ethernet delivered double-digit sequential and year-over-year growth with annualized revenue exceeding $10 billion.

evidence.claim: Sovereign AI revenue on track to exceed $20B this year, more than double last year.
evidence.quote: We are on track to achieve over $20 billion in sovereign AI revenue this year, more than double than that of last year.

evidence.claim: China market estimated at 'above $50 billion of opportunity' if addressable, growing ~50%/year.
evidence.quote: The China market I've estimated to be above $50 billion of opportunity for us this year. If we were able to address it with competitive products and if it's $50 billion this year, you would expect it to grow, say 50% per year, as the rest of the world's AI market is growing as well.
Blackwell is the AI platform the world has been waiting for... production of Blackwell Ultra is ramping at full speed, and demand is extraordinary. — Jensen Huang, press release.

evidence.claim: Long-term AI infrastructure opportunity $3–4 trillion by end of decade.
evidence.quote: We see $3 trillion to $4 trillion in AI infrastructure spend by the end of the decade.

evidence.claim: $60B share repurchase authorization added; $10B returned in Q2.
evidence.quote: Our Board of Directors recently approved a $60 billion share repurchase authorization to add to our remaining $14.7 billion of authorization at the end of Q2. While we prioritize funding our growth and strategic initiatives in Q2, we returned $10 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and cash dividends.

review_flags.reason: The score of 0.60 is based on a strong forward guidance raise and confident language, but the second consecutive Data Center optical miss and growth deceleration could be interpreted as more significant by the market. The manual baseline worksheet notes the stock actually opened down 0.43% the next day, suggesting the market's reaction was more muted than the score implies. A reviewer may wish to assess whether the Data Center miss should weigh more heavily.
